result.title: Neural Wasserstein Splines: Representation-Invariant Second-Order Priors for Trajectory Inference
result.summary: Population dynamics are often observed only as unpaired snapshots, which leave the evolution between measurements underdetermined. Second-order regularization can constrain it, but a penalty on the accelerations of sampled particles is a prior on joint particle paths, and different particle representations of the same marginal curve can have different acceleration costs. We therefore introduce Neural Wasserstein Splines (NWSP), a sample-based method that learns a continuous population curve under a Wasserstein smoothness prior. A neural network maps latent variables to the control points of a cubic spline in time, so samples at any time come from the spline basis without numerical integration. We project the generator's velocity onto gradients of a finite dictionary of scalar potentials and differentiate this measure-dependent projection in time, obtaining a finite-dimensional surrogate for the intrinsic Wasserstein acceleration, trained jointly with distributional fit losses. For a fixed dictionary and ridge parameter, we prove that the population penalty depends only on the marginal curve and bound its sensitivity to moment-estimation errors. Learned potentials (NWSP-N) sharpen acceleration estimates. On various synthetic and single-cell benchmarks, NWSP is highly competitive with transport and flow-based methods, ranking in the top two in 11 of 16 settings. The penalty improves on an unregularized spline in 13 of 16 settings and, while competitive with a particle-acceleration penalty, adds provable representation invariance.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Neural Wasserstein Splines（NWSP）：用神经网络把 latent 变量映射为三次样条控制点，从而无需数值积分即可在任意时刻采样，并以有限势函数字典上的速度投影逼近 Wasserstein 加速度作为二阶平滑先验，证明固定字典下该惩罚只依赖边缘曲线，在多组合成与单细胞基准上与传输/流方法相当。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「表示不变性」惩罚及对矩估计误差的敏感性界，可能为 LVR 中 latent 相似度与内部状态度量如何摆脱采样、位置或缓存表示依赖提供可核查的度量设计线索；latent 到连续时间样条轨迹的生成方式也可能类比 latent 推理状态的连续更新。
